Appearing on the “The Diary Of A CEO” podcast on June 30, 2025, O’Leary discussed the key attributes he looks for in employees.
“I find the ones that are eclectic people, that have other pursuits that are nothing to do with the business they’re in,” the “Shark” said.
O’Leary noted, for instance, that someone asking for days off to cycle in a desert is the sort of thing that attracts his attention.
“If you look at the year’s outcome from that person, you’re going to find that they probably outperformed,” he added.
O’Leary, also known as "Mr. Wonderful," refused to believe that people who work hard in a psychopathic way tend to succeed.
“You want the ones that are not just robots working,” he emphasized, adding that he’d opt for an actual robot in the future once they become available.
The Canadian tycoon said he prefers people with “creative” and “unusual solutions,” and who could think outside of the box.

Best known to American audiences as one of the original investors on the reality television show “Shark Tank,” O’Leary investment profile spans public equities, private equity, venture capital and cryptocurrencies, including
